```text
# marvin — Working Journal

Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for marvin. Newest entries at the top. For *what marvin is* (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones), read [`spec.md`](spec.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.

---

**UI architecture — nav drawer complete; song/mode-select dialog is the next UI step.** The canvas compositor + per-screen-module model is built and validated on hardware: `ui_manager` orchestrates screens (string table + `screenInit/Show`; the MGS screen state machine is disabled, worked around with the `compat/le_gen_init.h` stub), the dashboard is its own MGS Screen on BASE, and the nav drawer is its own MGS Screen (`Navigation`) re-hosted onto OVR1 — they coexist live (no active-screen gate; `leUpdate`/`leInput` cover all attached layers). `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3 is pinned via the never-shown `LayerBudget` screen. **Nav drawer is feature-complete:** slides in/out via canvas Move FX (`NAV_CLOSED_X` dodges the window-clip row-wrap; mid-slide reversal cancels the in-flight move), single-active highlight (Dashboard closes, others switch), clean close, rounded buttons with anti-aliased corners (`ui/widgets/button_aa/widget_button_aa.c`, per-instance vtable re-point — see `ui_compositor.md` §10a). Authoritative design + the window-clip/alignment gotchas in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md); decisions 2026-06-25. **Next:** author song/mode-select as its own MGS Screen, hosted by `ui_manager` on OVR2 as a modal (assign `canvas[2]` a buffer, re-host onto layer 2, dashboard live behind) — first coexist-with-live-background exercise; the re-host + slide mechanics are proven on the nav. Ties into the song_list widget below (the scrollable list goes inside that dialog). The earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable / reveal-then-promote" framing is **superseded** (a state-machine artifact).
```

```text
21	/* ui_manager is the UI orchestrator + compositor.
22	 *
23	 * Canvas vs. hardware layer: a canvas (CANVAS_* in ui_manager.h) is a RAM
24	 * surface a screen renders into; a hardware layer (HW_*) is what the LCDC scans
25	 * out. They are independent — ui_manager binds a canvas onto whatever HW layer
26	 * suits at the moment with gfxcSetLayer. A screen never owns a layer; the layer
27	 * is chosen here, at display time. Note gfxcSetLayer only takes effect while the
28	 * canvas is hidden, so layer binds always precede gfxcShowCanvas.
29	 *
30	 * Boot is two phases, run by the boot task once the scheduler is up:
31	 *   1. Splash — the splash module loads a raw RGBA8888 image off the SD straight
32	 *      into its canvas; we bind that canvas to SPLASH_HW_LAYER and light the
33	 *      backlight. No Legato. The splash-shown callback then lets the app start
34	 *      everything else in parallel.
35	 *   2. Screens — each MGS/Legato screen is built one at a time (they all build
36	 *      into Legato layer 0, so each is detached after init to free layer 0 for
37	 *      the next), then the active screens are bound to their display layers and
38	 *      paint behind the splash. After a minimum hold the splash is hidden,
39	 *      revealing the (warm) dashboard. */
40	
41	#define SPLASH_MIN_MS   5000u   /* hold the splash at least this long */
42	
43	/* Render-completion wait. leRenderer_IsIdle() is also true in the gaps between
44	 * leUpdate calls (LEGATO_Tasks ticks ~10 ms), so a single idle sample can read
45	 * "done" mid-paint. Require idle to hold continuously for a window several ticks
46	 * long before trusting it; bounded overall so a stall can't hang boot. */
47	#define RENDER_POLL_MS            5u
48	#define RENDER_IDLE_STABLE_MS   120u
49	#define RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS 8000u

89	/* GFX-canvas drvLayer index → XLCDC layer enum (the XLCDC poke namespace). */
90	static XLCDC_LAYER xlcdc_layer(uint32_t hw)
91	{
92	    switch (hw)
93	    {
94	        case HW_BASE: return XLCDC_LAYER_BASE;
95	        case HW_OVR2: return XLCDC_LAYER_OVR2;
96	        case HW_OVR1:
97	        default:      return XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1;
98	    }

101	/* Bind a canvas to a hardware layer and optionally show it. The GFX-XLCDC driver
102	 * never writes RGBMODE itself, so we poke the layer's colour mode to match the
103	 * canvas placed on it — the layer always follows its current canvas. gfxcSetLayer
104	 * requires the canvas hidden, which it is until shown. */
105	static void bind_canvas(uint32_t canvas, uint32_t hw, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE mode, bool show)
106	{
107	    gfxcSetLayer(canvas, hw);
108	    if (show) { gfxcShowCanvas(canvas); }
109	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(canvas);
110	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(xlcdc_layer(hw), mode, true);
111	}

113	static uint32_t s_backlight_pct;
114	
115	/* Set the backlight brightness (0–100%, clamped). The backlight is PWM-dimmed on
116	 * PC18 (PWM channel 0, configured by MCC), period read at runtime so this tracks
117	 * whatever MCC sets. The channel is CPOL_LOW — it idles low (dark) when stopped,
118	 * so the panel stays off until the splash — which means CDTY is the LOW-level
119	 * time and brightness is the high fraction: CDTY = period·(100−pct)/100, so
120	 * pct=100 → CDTY 0 → full bright, pct=0 → CDTY period → off. PWM_ChannelDutySet
121	 * writes CDTY directly while stopped and the update register once running, so
122	 * this is valid both before the channel starts and at runtime. */
123	void UiManager_SetBacklight(uint32_t pct)
124	{
125	    if (pct > 100u) { pct = 100u; }
126	    s_backlight_pct = pct;
127	    uint32_t period = PWM_ChannelPeriodGet(PWM_CHANNEL_0);
128	    PWM_ChannelDutySet(PWM_CHANNEL_0, (period * (100u - pct)) / 100u);
129	}
130	
131	uint32_t UiManager_GetBacklight(void)
132	{
133	    return s_backlight_pct;
134	}
135	
136	/* Light the backlight at the persisted brightness (Settings_Get loads the QSPI
137	 * ring on first use, or the compiled default if no record). The PWM channel is
138	 * stopped (no output) until started here, so the panel stays dark until the
139	 * splash is up — no pre-splash frame. PWM_Initialize ran at startup; this sets
140	 * the duty (while stopped, so the channel starts straight at the target) and
141	 * starts it. */
142	static void enable_backlight(void)
143	{
144	    UiManager_SetBacklight(Settings_Get()->backlight_pct);
145	    PWM_ChannelsStart(PWM_CHANNEL_0_MASK);
146	}

148	/* ── Legato render serialization ──────────────────────────────────────────────
149	 * leAddRootWidget/leRemoveRootWidget mutate Legato's per-layer root lists with no
150	 * locking, and LEGATO_Tasks + SYS_INPUT_Tasks (both run from scheduler start)
151	 * traverse those lists. The boot task edits the scene graph post-scheduler, so it
152	 * suspends those two readers around the edits. Safe to suspend here: at guard
153	 * time no app roots are attached (the splash is pure LCDC scanout), so the
154	 * renderer is idle; resuming hands rendering back. GFX_CANVAS_Tasks is left
155	 * running (it commits canvases; not a root-list reader). */
156	static TaskHandle_t s_legato_task;
157	static TaskHandle_t s_input_task;
158	
159	static void scene_edit_begin(void)
160	{
161	    s_legato_task = xTaskGetHandle("LEGATO_Tasks");
162	    s_input_task  = xTaskGetHandle("SYS_INPUT_Tasks");
163	    if (s_legato_task != NULL) { vTaskSuspend(s_legato_task); }
164	    if (s_input_task  != NULL) { vTaskSuspend(s_input_task);  }
165	    if (s_legato_task == NULL || s_input_task == NULL)
166	    {
167	        LOG_WARN("UI: render task handle not found; scene edit unguarded\r\n");
168	    }
169	}
170	
171	static void scene_edit_end(void)
172	{
173	    if (s_input_task  != NULL) { vTaskResume(s_input_task);  }
174	    if (s_legato_task != NULL) { vTaskResume(s_legato_task); }
175	}
176	
177	/* Build every screen and leave them all detached. They each build into Legato
178	 * layer 0, so detach each before the next so layer 0 is free to reuse. */
179	static void init_screens(void)
180	{
181	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < UI_SCREEN_COUNT; i++)
182	    {
183	        (void)s_screens[i].init();
184	        leRemoveRootWidget(s_screens[i].get_root(0), 0);
185	    }
186	}
187	
188	/* Block until the Legato render task has painted all pending damage. We don't
189	 * drive leUpdate — LEGATO_Tasks + GFX_CANVAS_Task render correctly when they run;
190	 * we just yield and poll the public idle flag, requiring it to hold continuously
191	 * (a lone idle sample is an inter-frame gap, not a finished paint). Bounded. */
192	static void wait_render_idle(void)
193	{
194	    TickType_t deadline   = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS);
195	    TickType_t idle_since = 0;
196	    bool       idle_run   = false;
197	
198	    while (xTaskGetTickCount() < deadline)
199	    {
200	        if (leRenderer_IsIdle())
201	        {
202	            if (!idle_run)
203	            {
204	                idle_run   = true;
205	                idle_since = xTaskGetTickCount();
206	            }
207	            else if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - idle_since) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_STABLE_MS))
208	            {
209	                return;
210	            }
211	        }
212	        else
213	        {
214	            idle_run = false;
215	        }
216	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_POLL_MS));
217	    }
218	    LOG_WARN("UI: render-idle wait timed out\r\n");
219	}
220	
221	/* ── boot sequence ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
222	
223	static void ui_boot_task(void *param)
224	{
225	    (void)param;
226	
227	    /* PHASE 1 — splash, before any Legato work, as fast as the SD allows. */
228	    (void)Splash_Load();   /* loads the image, or fills the fallback colour */
229	    bind_canvas(Splash_CanvasId(), SPLASH_HW_LAYER, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, true);
230	    enable_backlight();
231	    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();
232	
233	    /* Splash is up — let the app start everything else (services + camera) now,
234	     * in parallel with the screen painting below, so it's all warm at reveal. */
235	    if (s_splash_shown_cb != NULL) { s_splash_shown_cb(); }
236	
237	    /* PHASE 2 — build + host the Legato screens behind the splash. Scene-graph
238	     * edits are guarded against the render tasks; the canvas/layer binds after
239	     * are GFX-canvas only (no root-list mutation) so they need no guard. */
240	    scene_edit_begin();
241	    init_screens();
242	    s_screens[UI_SCREEN_DASHBOARD].host();
243	    s_screens[UI_SCREEN_NAV].host();
244	    scene_edit_end();
245	
246	    /* Dashboard live on BASE (covered by the splash until reveal). The nav is
247	     * hosted + painting into its own canvas, but not bound to a layer yet — it
248	     * shares OVR1 with the splash, so it takes OVR1 only after the splash vacates
249	     * it at reveal. */
250	    bind_canvas(CANVAS_DASH, HW_BASE, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, true);
251	
252	    wait_render_idle();
253	
254	    /* Hold the splash a minimum time so a fast boot doesn't flash it away. */
255	    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
256	    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
257	    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }
258	
259	    /* REVEAL — cut over to the (painted) dashboard, then give the nav OVR1. */
260	    gfxcHideCanvas(Splash_CanvasId());
261	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(Splash_CanvasId());
262	    bind_canvas(CANVAS_NAV, HW_OVR1, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, false);
263	
264	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
265	}
266	
267	/* ── screen host hooks ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
268	 * Attach the screen's root onto its own canvas and set its window/content. No
269	 * layer bind, no show — the compositor decides the layer and visibility. (The nav
270	 * has its own host hook, Navigation_OnShow, in screen_nav.c.) */
271	void Dashboard_OnShow(void)
272	{
273	    leWidget *root = screenGetRoot_Dashboard(0);
274	    leAddRootWidget(root, CANVAS_DASH);
275	    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_DASH, 0, 0);
276	    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_DASH, BASE_W, BASE_H);
277	    root->fn->invalidate(root);
278	}
279	
280	/* ── public API ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

282	void UiManager_Initialize(void)
283	{
284	    /* Assign the per-screen canvas surfaces, then drive the canvas state machine
285	     * to RUNNING so a blit isn't dropped by the RUNNING gate, then set the Legato
286	     * string table the screens need. All pre-scheduler config — no screen built
287	     * or shown here; the boot task does the sequence. */
288	    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_DASH, BASE_W, BASE_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, s_fb_base);
289	    Splash_InitSurface();
290	    Nav_InitSurface();
291	    GFX_CANVAS_Task();
292	
293	    leSetStringTable(&stringTable);
294	    initializeStrings();
295	
296	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(ui_boot_task, "UiBoot", BOOT_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
297	                            NULL, BOOT_TASK_PRIORITY, s_boot_stack, &s_boot_tcb);
298	}
```

```text
14	
15	/* The nav drawer is authored as its own MGS Screen (Navigation) and renders into
16	 * its own canvas (CANVAS_NAV, defined in ui_manager.h). The nav is layer-agnostic
17	 * — ui_manager (the compositor) decides which hardware layer this canvas is shown
18	 * on; the drawer's slide works on the canvas window, independent of the layer. */
19	#define NAV_W   320u
20	#define NAV_H   800u
21	
22	/* gfxcStartEffectMove delta — slide feel (DEC = ease-out). Tune to taste. */
23	#define NAV_SLIDE_DELTA  6u
24	
25	/* Off-screen-left X for the closed drawer / slide-out target.
26	 *
27	 * A canvas layer can't truly sit off-screen — the window-clip (gfx_canvas.c
28	 * _gfxcCanvasUpdate) emulates a negative X by shifting the source pointer right
29	 * and shrinking the window. But it first aligns X *down* to a multiple of
30	 * CANVAS_WIN_X_ALIGN (`x &= ~0x3` for non-32bpp surfaces), and once |X| reaches
31	 * the surface width the shifted pointer wraps to the next row, flashing the
32	 * panel's left columns through. So the furthest the drawer can validly sit is
33	 * the largest aligned X with |X| < NAV_W. We slide to there; nav_fx_done then
34	 * disables the layer, clearing the residual edge sliver. Derived from NAV_W so
35	 * it tracks the surface width, not a hard-coded pixel count. */
36	#define CANVAS_WIN_X_ALIGN  4u   /* mirrors the clip's `x &= ~0x3` */
37	#define NAV_CLOSED_X        (-(int)((NAV_W - 1u) & ~(CANVAS_WIN_X_ALIGN - 1u)))
38	
39	/* Rounded button corners. The widget cornerRadius is honored by the classic
40	 * skin's background draw but isn't exposed in MGS, so we set it in code. */
41	#define NAV_CORNER_RADIUS  12u
42	
43	#define FB_NOCACHE   __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned (32)))
44	
45	static uint16_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_nav[NAV_W * NAV_H];
46	
47	static bool s_nav_open = false;
48	
49	/* Navigation entries, in panel order. The selected one is the active screen. */
50	#define NAV_COUNT  6u
51	
52	static leButtonWidget *nav_button(unsigned int i)
53	{
54	    switch (i)
55	    {
56	        case 0:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD;
57	        case 1:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_LOGS;
58	        case 2:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_PERFORMANCE;
59	        case 3:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_SYSTEM_INFO;
60	        case 4:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DIAGNOSTICS;
61	        default: return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_SETTINGS;
62	    }
63	}
64	
65	static void nav_close(void);   /* forward decl — nav_on_release may close the drawer */
66	
67	/* Single-active highlight: paint the active entry selected, the rest unselected. */
68	static void nav_highlight(leButtonWidget *active)
69	{
70	    unsigned int i;
71	
72	    for (i = 0u; i < NAV_COUNT; i++)
73	    {
74	        leButtonWidget *b = nav_button(i);
75	        b->fn->setScheme(b, (b == active) ? &SCHEME_NAV_BUTTON_SELECTED
76	                                          : &SCHEME_NAV_BUTTON_UNSELECTED);
77	    }
78	}
79	
80	/* Released-event sink for every nav entry. Switch the highlight; Dashboard means
81	 * "back to the main view" so it also closes the drawer, while the other entries
82	 * just change the selection and stay open. The active screen-switch will hook
83	 * here once the per-screen canvas model lands. */
84	static void nav_on_release(leButtonWidget *btn)
85	{
86	    nav_highlight(btn);
87	
88	    if (btn == Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD)
89	    {
90	        nav_close();
91	    }
92	}
93	
94	static void nav_buttons_init(void)
95	{
96	    unsigned int i;
97	
98	    /* Route every nav-entry release through nav_on_release (runtime-registered
99	     * here — the Navigation screen wires no button events itself) and round the
100	     * corners (not an MGS option). */
101	    for (i = 0u; i < NAV_COUNT; i++)
102	    {
103	        nav_button(i)->fn->setReleasedEventCallback(nav_button(i), nav_on_release);
104	        nav_button(i)->fn->setCornerRadius(nav_button(i), NAV_CORNER_RADIUS);
105	        ButtonAA_Enable(nav_button(i));
106	    }
107	
108	    /* Dashboard is the active entry at startup — set the highlight only (calling
109	     * the release sink here would close the not-yet-open drawer). */
110	    nav_highlight(Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD);
111	}
112	
113	/* Animate the drawer to target_x from wherever it currently sits. Cancel any
114	 * in-flight slide first: gfxcStartEffectMove is a no-op while a move is running
115	 * (it only starts from status IDLE), so without the stop a mid-slide reversal
116	 * would be silently dropped — the original move would run to completion and fire
117	 * nav_fx_done with a now-stale s_nav_open, hiding the drawer and wedging the
118	 * toggle. Reading the live position makes the reversal retarget smoothly. */
119	static void nav_slide_to(int target_x)
120	{
121	    int x, y;
122	
123	    gfxcStopEffect(CANVAS_NAV, GFXC_FX_MOVE);
124	    gfxcGetWindowPosition(CANVAS_NAV, &x, &y);
125	    gfxcStartEffectMove(CANVAS_NAV, GFXC_FX_MOVE_DEC, x, 0, target_x, 0, NAV_SLIDE_DELTA);
126	}
127	
128	static void nav_open(void)
129	{
130	    /* Force a full repaint of the panel into the canvas before revealing it — the
131	     * paint queued at startup (parked off-screen) doesn't fully land in the
132	     * buffer, so without this the drawer slides in partially drawn until touch
133	     * damage fills it in. The repaint lands over the next frames as it slides.
134	     * Show first so the move is visible (the FX engine enables the layer from
135	     * canvas.active). */
136	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->invalidate(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION);
137	    gfxcShowCanvas(CANVAS_NAV);
138	    nav_slide_to(0);
139	    s_nav_open = true;
140	}
141	
142	static void nav_close(void)
143	{
144	    /* Slide out to NAV_CLOSED_X (off-screen), then nav_fx_done disables the
145	     * layer. NAV_CLOSED_X avoids the -NAV_W window-clip row-wrap (see its
146	     * definition); the layer update busy-waits for the vsync latch, so the final
147	     * frame is displayed before the hide lands — keeping it in-bounds makes that
148	     * frame a harmless edge sliver instead of the panel's left columns. */
149	    nav_slide_to(NAV_CLOSED_X);
150	    s_nav_open = false;
151	}
152	
153	/* Move-effect completion callback. At the off-screen end of a close slide the
154	 * window clip leaves a degenerate sliver of the drawer composited at screen
155	 * left; hiding the canvas (disabling its layer) once the slide finishes removes it cleanly. Only
156	 * acts on a completed close — an open leaves the layer shown, and a re-open
157	 * mid-close restarts the move (so this won't fire for the abandoned close). */
158	static void nav_fx_done(unsigned int canvasID, GFXC_FX_TYPE effect,
159	                        GFXC_FX_STATUS status, void *parm)
160	{
161	    (void)canvasID;
162	    (void)parm;
163	
164	    if (effect == GFXC_FX_MOVE && status == GFXC_FX_DONE && !s_nav_open)
165	    {
166	        gfxcHideCanvas(CANVAS_NAV);
167	        gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_NAV);
168	    }
169	}
170	
171	void Nav_InitSurface(void)
172	{
173	    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_NAV, NAV_W, NAV_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, s_fb_nav);
174	}
175	
176	/* Host hook for the Navigation screen (declared in le_gen_screen_Navigation.h).
177	 * The MGS screen authors its content on Legato layer 0; move the root so it
178	 * renders into CANVAS_NAV instead (the dashboard keeps canvas 0), set the window
179	 * (parked off-screen / closed) and content. Layer-agnostic — ui_manager binds
180	 * CANVAS_NAV to a hardware layer; the canvas update there applies this window.
181	 * Keep the panel visible+enabled so Legato renders it continuously, and start
182	 * closed: the touch pick rect follows the canvas window position
183	 * (LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE), so a closed (off-screen) nav can't intercept dashboard
184	 * touches, and the off-screen X seeds the slide-in. */
185	void Navigation_OnShow(void)
186	{
187	    leWidget *root = screenGetRoot_Navigation(0);
188	    leRemoveRootWidget(root, 0);
189	    leAddRootWidget(root, CANVAS_NAV);
190	
191	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->setEnabled(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION, LE_TRUE);
192	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->setVisible(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION, LE_TRUE);
193	
194	    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_NAV, NAV_W, NAV_H);
195	    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_NAV, NAV_CLOSED_X, 0);
196	    gfxcSetEffectsCallback(CANVAS_NAV, nav_fx_done, NULL);
197	
198	    nav_buttons_init();
199	}
200	
201	/* Hamburger on the Dashboard screen (BASE) toggles the nav drawer. */
202	void event_Dashboard_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION_OnPressed(leButtonWidget* btn)
203	{
204	    (void)btn;
205	    if (s_nav_open) { nav_close(); } else { nav_open(); }
206	}
```

99	Each panel is authored as its own **1-layer** MGS screen, so nothing reaches 3 layers on its own —

107	### 4.3 Why HEO is safe (and stays enabled)
108	Layer targeting is **explicit, not positional**: Legato layer *i* → `canvas[i]` →
109	`gfxcSetLayer(i, hwLayer)`, where `hwLayer` indexes `layerOrder`. We map canvases only to hw layers
110	**0 / 2 / 3** (BASE / OVR1 / OVR2) and **never to 1 (HEO)**, so the canvas framework never issues an
111	IOCTL to HEO regardless of enumeration order. The only GFX-side touch of HEO is
112	`DRV_XLCDC_Initialize` disabling all enumerated layers once at init — before `video.c` configures it
113	(post-scheduler), so video is the last writer. So **HEO stays enabled** and `video.c` keeps full
114	runtime control via the XLCDC PLIB, including the `HEOCFG12` blender + `VIDPRI` z-order that
115	`XLCDC_SetupHEOLayer` provides (`video.c` does not set those itself — which is exactly why disabling
116	HEO in MCC would break compositing, and why we don't).

118	## 5. Live coexistence vs. replacement
119	
120	The compositor offers two verbs, chosen per interaction — you do **not** pick one global mode:
121	
122	- **Coexist (overlay-as-layer)** — the panel is its own layer over a still-live background.
123	  Used for the **nav drawer** (dashboard keeps updating behind it) and the **modal dialog**
124	  (telemetry keeps updating around it). No freeze.
125	- **Replace (switch base view)** — a full-screen view replaces another on layer 0; the
126	  outgoing one detaches (its surface can hold the last frame, or it is rebuilt on return).
127	  Used when a view genuinely supersedes the dashboard and live background isn't needed.
128	
129	Because the compositor owns layer placement and attach/detach, moving an interaction between
130	these is a compositor-level change, not a per-module rewrite — the reversibility we wanted.

145	```

151	- **Per-screen/overlay modules** own only their panel's content + event wiring, registered

You're right, and that's an important correction — I conflated two separate namespaces. Re-reading §4.3:

> Layer targeting is **explicit, not positional**: Legato layer *i* → `canvas[i]` → `gfxcSetLayer(i, hwLayer)`, where `hwLayer` indexes `layerOrder`.

So the second arg to `leAddRootWidget` is a **Legato layer index**, and the GFX canvas framework maps Legato layer *i* → `canvas[i]` by deliberate design (you keep the numbering aligned so the mapping is 1:1 and clean), not because the canvas id "is" a layer. And the canvas→HW-layer binding is a third, independent choice made at display time via `gfxcSetLayer`. Three namespaces, kept aligned on purpose.

That also corrects my LE_LAYER_COUNT worry. The whole point of pinning it at **3** (§4.2) is that Legato manages exactly layers 0/1/2, and SongSelect is meant to be the **third** one — no bump needed:

| Screen | Legato layer | Canvas | HW layer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dashboard | 0 | `canvas[0]` (CANVAS_DASH) | BASE |
| Nav | 1 | `canvas[1]` (CANVAS_NAV) | OVR1 |
| **SongSelect** | **2** | **`canvas[2]`** | **OVR2** |

And `canvas[2]` is currently `CANVAS_SPLASH` — the splash uses it as a pure-LCDC scanout surface (no Legato root). §7-Next-1 spells out exactly this: *"assign `canvas[2]` a real buffer and have `ui_manager` host it on layer 2 (OVR2)."* After the splash is hidden at reveal, that canvas slot is free to repoint to a SongSelect RGB565 buffer and attach the SongSelect Legato root to layer 2.

```text
10	In marvin's Legato/GFX_CANVAS UI, canvases and screens do **not** own a hardware layer. MGS-generated code builds every screen into Legato **layer 0** by default; `UiManager` disconnects it from layer 0 after build (`leRemoveRootWidget`). A canvas is bound to a specific hardware layer (BASE / OVR1 / OVR2) via `gfxcSetLayer` **only when it needs to be displayed**, and that binding is transient and reassignable. We avoid leaving screens on layer 0 at init solely because layer 0 is MGS's default build target — not an ownership claim.
11	
12	**Why:** I have repeatedly mis-reasoned that "nav is on OVR1" or "splash is on OVR2" are fixed assignments that conflict. They are not — two canvases that are never shown at the same time can use the same hardware layer; whoever binds it at display time wins.
13	
14	A screen owns its **canvas** (render surface); which **hardware layer** that canvas is shown on is a runtime decision made by the compositor/policy (`ui_manager`), via `gfxcSetLayer` at display time. Nav typically ends up on OVR1 — but that is a choice, NOT a property of the nav. Never write code or comments that treat "nav == OVR1" (or any screen == a layer) as fixed. Layer assignment lives in `ui_manager` (e.g. `UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(id, hw_layer)`), never in a screen module and never in a boot/loader path.
15	
16	**How to apply:** When changing which HW layer a screen displays on, just rebind at display time and don't treat another screen's current layer use as a blocking conflict. Check the display-time sequence (who calls `gfxcSetLayer`/`gfxcShowCanvas` when), not init-time "ownership." The user has corrected this repeatedly — do not regress. Related: [[marvin-journal]].
```

```md
The lifecycle of a marvin UI screen (the user has corrected me on this MANY times — do not regress):

1. **Every MGS screen is authored with a single layer.** MGS builds each screen into **layer 0** — that is just MGS's build target, not an ownership claim.
2. **At startup `ui_manager` generates the screens one by one**, each onto layer 0, then **disconnects it from that setup layer** (`leRemoveRootWidget(root, 0)`).
3. After the disconnect the screen is an **independent canvas**: it owns a render surface and is attached to **no hardware layer**.
4. **The canvas is bound to a hardware layer (BASE / OVR1 / OVR2) at display time, at runtime, via `gfxcSetLayer(canvasID, hwLayer)`** — a `ui_manager` policy decision that is **transient and reassignable**. The same canvas can be on OVR1 in one situation and OVR2 in another.

**canvas id ≠ hardware layer.** They are different namespaces and NEITHER is a fixed property of the screen. Do NOT write code, comments, tables, or prose that say "nav == OVR1", "splash == OVR2", "SongSelect is the OVR2 screen", or that a canvas id "doubles as" / "is" a layer. Which HW layer a canvas shows on is decided only at display time by whoever calls `gfxcSetLayer`/`gfxcShowCanvas`.

**Why it matters:** two canvases never shown at the same time can share one HW layer — whoever binds it at display time wins. So another screen's *current* layer use is not a blocking conflict. The HW-layer budget limits how many canvases are *visible at once*, not how many screens exist.

**How to apply:** to change which HW layer a screen displays on, just rebind at display time; don't treat another screen's layer use as fixed. Layer-binding policy lives in `ui_manager`, never in a screen module or boot/loader path. When reasoning about a new screen, the questions are "which canvas does it own?" and "which free HW layer does ui_manager bind it to *when shown*?" — never "which layer does it own?". Related: [[marvin-journal]], `firmware/marvin/docs/ui_compositor.md` §4.3.
```

```text
static gfxResult GFXC_BufferBlit(const gfxPixelBuffer* source,
                            const gfxRect* rectSrc,
                            const gfxPixelBuffer* dest,
                            const gfxRect* rectDest)
{
    void* srcPtr;
    void* destPtr;
    uint32_t row, rowSize;
    unsigned int width, height;
    gfxResult res = GFX_FAILURE;

#if (CONFIG_CANVAS_GPU_BLIT_ENABLE == true)
    res = gfxcGPU->blitBuffer(source,
                              rectSrc,
                              dest,
                              rectDest);
#endif

    if (res != GFX_SUCCESS)
    {
        width = (rectSrc->width < rectDest->width) ?
                    rectSrc->width : rectDest->width;
        height = (rectSrc->height < rectDest->height) ?
                    rectSrc->height : rectDest->height;
        rowSize = width * gfxColorInfoTable[dest->mode].size;

        for(row = 0; row < height; row++)
        {
            srcPtr = gfxPixelBufferOffsetGet(source, rectSrc->x, rectSrc->y + row);
            destPtr = gfxPixelBufferOffsetGet(dest, rectDest->x, rectDest->y + row);

            memcpy(destPtr, srcPtr, rowSize);
        }
    }

    return GFX_SUCCESS;
}

gfxResult GFXC_BlitBuffer(int32_t x,
                          int32_t y,
                          gfxPixelBuffer* buf)
{
    gfxRect srcRect, destRect;

	if (gfxcState != GFXC_RUNNING)
	{
		return GFX_FAILURE;
	}

	srcRect.x = 0;
    srcRect.y = 0;
    srcRect.height = buf->size.height;
    srcRect.width = buf->size.width;

    destRect.x = x;
    destRect.y = y;
    destRect.height = buf->size.height;
    destRect.width = buf->size.width;

	GFXC_BufferBlit(buf,
					&srcRect,
					&canvas[baseCanvasID + activeCanvasID].pixelBuffer,
					&destRect);


    return GFX_SUCCESS;
}

GFXC_RESULT _gfxcCopyBuffer(unsigned int srcID,
                         unsigned int destID,
                         const gfxRect * srcRect,
                         const gfxRect * destRect)
```

```text
# MGS Screens, Legato Layers, and GFX Canvases

## Architecture Overview

Yes, MGS recommends this approach. The documentation describes a single-screen project structure: **"MGS Harmony Composer will be a single-screen project with multiple layers. Each layer represents a logical screen in the GUI, which we will refer to as a layer-screen."**

## How Components Map Together

The relationship flows as follows:

1. **Design Phase**: Each GUI screen becomes a Legato layer within one master screen in MGS Harmony Composer
2. **Runtime Phase**: **"Each layer-screen in MGS Harmony Composer will be associated with a GFX Canvas object."** Each canvas receives its own dedicated frame buffer in RAM
3. **Display Phase**: **"The application will use the GFX Canvas Application Programming Interface (APIs) to show or hide layer-screens by assigning a layer or overlay in the LCD controller"**

## Key Architectural Principle

The system separates design concerns from display control. The layers exist persistently in memory as pre-rendered content, while canvases act as managers that determine what the LCD controller displays. As the guide explains: **"The LCD controller will display and composite the visible layer-screens on the display."**

This approach enables rapid screen transitions without redrawing, since **"Widget states are preserved during layer-screen transitions."**
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-29 21:37:00Z)**_

Read it. That doc is the key, and it reframes our whole back-and-forth. Here's my honest assessment.

## What the doc actually says

Microchip's intended model is a **single master MGS screen** whose **layers** are the things you and I call "screens":

- *"MGS Harmony Composer will be a single-screen project with multiple layers. Each layer represents a logical screen in the GUI… a layer-screen."*
- *"Each layer-screen… will be associated with a GFX Canvas object"* — its own framebuffer.
- *"The application will use the GFX Canvas APIs to show or hide layer-screens by assigning a layer or overlay in the LCD controller."*

So there are **three** concepts, not two:

| Concept | What it is | Coupling |
|---|---|---|
| **Legato layer** ("layer-screen") | a logical screen | 1:1 with a canvas |
| **GFX canvas** | the RAM framebuffer | tied to its Legato layer; **independent of HW layer** |
| **XLCDC HW layer** (BASE/OVR1/OVR2) | where it's composited | runtime, `gfxcSetLayer`, reassignable |

So your long-held belief was *right about HW layers and wrong about Legato layers* — exactly as you now suspect. canvas[i] ↔ Legato layer i are bound by design; the canvas→**HW**-layer mapping is the free, runtime one. That's why I kept hitting the `leAddRootWidget(root, layerIdx<3)` / `canvas[base+layerIdx]` wall: in this framework the canvas *is* the Legato layer's buffer.

And your "8 canvases, canvas id > LE_LAYER_COUNT doesn't matter" reconciles cleanly under this model: you can define up to **8 layer-screens** (so `LE_LAYER_COUNT` would be 8, canvases 0–7), and the LCDC just composites **any 3** of them onto its 3 usable HW layers at a time. Define many, show a few.

## Where marvin diverged (the source of our friction)

The current codebase does **not** follow the layer-screen model. Each panel is its own **separate MGS Screen** (`screen_Dashboard`, `screen_Navigation`, `screen_SongSelect`, `screen_LayerBudget`), each authored as a **1-layer** screen that builds into Legato layer 0. `ui_manager` then *manually* disconnects each root from layer 0 and re-hosts it onto layer 1/2 via `leRemoveRootWidget`/`leAddRootWidget`, and `LE_LAYER_COUNT` is pinned to 3 by the fake `LayerBudget` screen (`ui_compositor.md` §4.2).

That works (nav + dashboard coexist), but it's swimming upstream against the tooling — and it's precisely why "each screen gets its own canvas id" *can't* currently be true past slot 2: with `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3 there are only 3 Legato layers, so only canvases 0/1/2 are real render targets, and a 3rd live screen is forced onto slot 2 (the splash's).

## My recommendation

The doc's model *is* designed for marvin's exact need — several coexisting overlays with preserved widget state and no redraw on transition. I'd move toward it. Three options:

1. **Adopt the layer-screen model (best long-term).** Re-author in MGS Composer as one master screen with one layer per panel (Dashboard, Nav, SongSelect, …). MGS then derives `LE_LAYER_COUNT` from the layer count, each panel auto-associates with its own canvas, the `LayerBudget` hack and the manual disconnect/re-host dance both disappear, and "SongSelect owns canvas 3" becomes literally true. Cost: redo the MGS design + a regen; `ui_manager` gets *simpler*.
2. **Minimal unblock, same architecture.** Keep separate Screens but raise the layer budget (a 4-layer `LayerBudget`, or just author SongSelect as part of the pin) so `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=4 and SongSelect gets Legato layer 3 → canvas 3. Less clean, keeps the manual re-hosting.
3. **Ship the milestone as-is.** Under today's `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3, put SongSelect on Legato layer 2 → canvas 2 with its own RGB565 buffer, bound to OVR2 over the live dashboard. Gets it on screen now; revisit the model later.

I lean **#1** — it's the framework's intended path, matches your mental model exactly, and deletes the two biggest hacks we're carrying. But it's the kind of architectural call that belongs in the marvin journal/spec, and it touches the MGS design, so I want your decision before I touch anything.

Want me to spike #1 (sketch the master-screen/layer layout + what `ui_manager` becomes) so you can see the shape before committing, or just unblock SongSelect via #3 today and schedule the migration?

```md
THREE concepts in marvin's Legato/GFX_CANVAS UI — do not collapse them (the user has corrected me many times):

1. **Legato layer ("layer-screen")** — a logical screen/dialog/overlay. In MGS's intended model this is a *layer* on ONE master screen (per Microchip's GFX-canvas layer-screen guide). Bounded by `LE_LAYER_COUNT` = number of layer-screens.
2. **GFX canvas** — the RAM framebuffer backing a layer-screen. **Coupled 1:1 to its Legato layer**: the renderer writes Legato layer *i* into `canvas[baseCanvasID + i]` (base=0 → layer i ↔ canvas i). `leAddRootWidget(root, layerIdx)` rejects `layerIdx >= LE_LAYER_COUNT`. So canvas id is NOT free of the Legato layer — that was my repeated error.
3. **XLCDC hardware layer** (BASE/OVR1/OVR2; HEO=camera) — where a canvas is composited for scanout. Bound at **display time, at runtime, reassignable**, via `gfxcSetLayer(canvasID, hwLayer)` (see `ui_manager.c` `bind_canvas`). A canvas/screen does NOT own a HW layer; the same canvas can be on OVR1 in one situation, OVR2 in another.

**"canvas ≠ layer" is true ONLY for the HW layer (concept 3), NOT for the Legato layer (concept 2).** The 8-slot canvas pool (`CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ=8`) means you can define up to 8 layer-screens (so `LE_LAYER_COUNT` up to 8, canvases 0–7); the LCDC then composites **any 3** of them onto its 3 usable HW layers at once. "Define many, show a few." canvas id > current LE_LAYER_COUNT only becomes valid once LE_LAYER_COUNT grows to include it.

**Decided direction (2026-06-29):** migrate from the current "each panel is its own 1-layer MGS Screen, manually re-hosted by `ui_manager`, LE_LAYER_COUNT pinned at 3 by a fake LayerBudget screen" to the framework's model: **ONE master Legato screen named "Marvin" with one layer per panel** (dashboard, nav, song-select, dialogs…). MGS then derives LE_LAYER_COUNT and auto-associates each layer-screen with a canvas; the LayerBudget hack and the disconnect/re-host dance both go away. **Splash stays separate/manual** (pre-Legato RGBA8888 scanout) on a canvas slot OUTSIDE the layer-screen range.

**How to apply:** never write code/comments/tables that say a screen "owns" or "is" a HW layer — HW binding is `ui_manager`'s runtime `gfxcSetLayer` decision. But DO respect that a layer-screen's canvas is its Legato layer's buffer. Related: [[marvin-journal]], `firmware/marvin/docs/ui_compositor.md`, Microchip MGS layer-screen guide.
```

Memory fixed. Now the code side — here's what the migration to a single **"Marvin"** master screen means for our hand-written UI layer, and what I'll need from your MGS design.

## What gets simpler (the hacks that disappear)

The whole reason `ui_manager` is complicated today is that it's *emulating* layer-screens by hand:

- **`init_screens()` build-on-layer-0-then-disconnect loop** → gone. `screenInit_Marvin()` builds every layer-screen directly onto its own Legato layer / canvas. No `leRemoveRootWidget(root, 0)` dance.
- **Per-screen `*_OnShow` re-host hooks** (`Dashboard_OnShow`, `Navigation_OnShow` doing `leAddRootWidget(root, CANVAS_x)`) → gone. Roots are already placed by MGS.
- **`LayerBudget` fake screen + `compat/le_gen_init.h` stub** → gone. `LE_LAYER_COUNT` is now derived from Marvin's layer count.

## What `ui_manager` becomes

A thin compositor over the Marvin screen:

1. **Buffer assignment** — one `gfxcSetPixelBuffer(canvas_i, w_i, h_i, RGB565, buf_i)` per layer-screen, each canvas **sized to its content** (dashboard 1280×800, nav 320×800, song-select 1100×660) and positioned with the canvas window — exactly the pattern the nav already proves. Keeps DDR down vs. N full-screen buffers.
2. **`screenInit_Marvin()` once**, then call each panel module's setup fn.
3. **Clean show/hide verbs** the FX builds on:
   - `show_layer(layerIdx, hwLayer)` → `gfxcSetLayer(canvas, hw)` + `gfxcShowCanvas` + color mode
   - `hide_layer(layerIdx)` → `gfxcHideCanvas`
   - HW-layer choice stays a runtime `ui_manager` decision (never owned by a panel).

## What the panel modules become

`screen_nav.c`, `screen_song_select.c`, (new) `screen_dashboard.c` keep their **content + event wiring + interaction FX** (button callbacks, corner radius, nav slide, modal show), but **drop all canvas/layer mechanics** — no more `leAddRootWidget`. They operate on widgets MGS already placed on their layer. ui_manager calls each module's `*_Setup()` once after init.

## Splash — unchanged, one tweak

Stays manual/pre-Legato as discussed; just **move its canvas off slot 2** to the top of the pool (e.g. canvas 7) so it can't collide with Marvin's auto-assigned layer-screen canvases `0..N-1`.

## What I need from the "Marvin" design to write the code

1. **Layer order = Legato layer index = z-order (bottom→top).** I'm assuming `0 = Dashboard` (persistent base), then nav, then dialogs above. Confirm the order and the **initial set of layers** (Dashboard, Nav, SongSelect for now? do the other nav destinations — logs/settings/diagnostics — become layer-screens too, or render into the base layer?).
2. **Canvas sizing/association per layer-screen** — can each layer-screen carry a content-sized canvas + offset (like nav today), or does MGS force full-screen canvases? Affects buffers and the window-position math.
3. **Widget naming across layers** — how MGS names widgets in one multi-layer screen (e.g. `Marvin_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD` vs. today's `Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD`). That drives a rename sweep through the panel modules; I'll adapt once I see the generated `le_gen_assets.h`.
4. **Touch picking** — I'll need to confirm a hidden/off-screen layer-screen's canvas suppresses input picking (the nav relies on this via off-screen window). Likely fine, but it's the one behavior I'll validate on hardware.

If that lines up with your thinking, I'll write this into the marvin journal as the migration plan (phased: regen Marvin design → strip `ui_manager` to the verbs → port nav → bring up SongSelect as a real layer-screen → delete LayerBudget/compat stub), so it survives the regen churn. 11	(dashboard on BASE + slide-in nav on OVR1, single-active highlight). **Next: the `ui_manager`
```text
12	+ per-screen-module refactor** described in §6–§7.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. The core idea
17	
18	Content geometry was welded to hardware 1:1:1 — one Legato layer → one framebuffer → one LCDC
19	layer. There are only **4 LCDC layers** (`BASE`, `OVR1`, `HEO`, `OVR2`); `HEO` is the live
20	camera. The compositor breaks the welding:
21	
22	- A **surface** is a RAM framebuffer (a GFX Canvas object) holding a panel's pixels.
23	- A **layer** is a hardware compositor window. The LCDC blends them every scan with zero CPU.
24	- Showing a panel = point a layer at its surface + enable (register writes, no re-render).
25	  Hiding = disable/move the layer. Sliding = animate the layer's window position.
26	
27	**GFX Canvas** is the substrate: `GFXC_GetPixelBuffer` redirects Legato's render target to a
28	canvas object, and `gfxcSetLayer`/`ShowCanvas`/`SetWindowPosition` map/show/move that surface
29	on an LCDC layer. (Why canvas and not a hand-rolled retarget or direct-layer-only: see the
30	2026-06-25 journal entry — canvas is the only thing that gets Legato content *into* an
31	arbitrary off-screen surface; direct layer control still does the show/move.)
32	
33	## 2. The enabling change — MGS screen state machine OFF
34	
35	Legato's stock "screen state machine" (`le_gen_init.c`) shows **one screen at a time** —
36	`legato_showScreen` tears down the outgoing screen's widget tree. That is fatal to a compositor
37	that wants several panels live simultaneously. So it is **disabled** ("Generate Screen State
38	Machine" off; `le_gen_init.{c,h}` no longer generated — see the 2026-06-25 journal entry and
39	the `compat/` stub that works around the resulting MGS include bug).
40	
41	Two confirmed facts make this work (verified in `legato_state.c` / `legato_renderer.c` /
42	`legato_input.c`):
43	
44	1. **`_state.layerList` is global and `leUpdate` renders/updates *every* attached layer each
45	   frame.** There is no "active screen" render gate. Attach roots to multiple layers → they all
46	   render live.
47	2. **Touch picks across all attached layers, top-to-bottom** (`leInput` iterates `layerList`
48	   from the top). So an attached overlay is interactive wherever it sits; the layer below
49	   receives touches elsewhere. *(This supersedes the earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable /
50	   reveal-then-promote" idea — that was a consequence of the state machine, which is now gone.)*
51	
52	So the model is simply: **attach a panel's root to a layer → it is live and interactive;
53	detach (or move off-screen) → it is gone.** No freeze, no promotion dance.
54	
55	## 3. MGS Screen = widget-tree factory
56	
57	With the state machine off, the generated per-screen functions are ours to call directly
58	(MGS even relabels them `// call to show this screen`). We treat each **MGS Screen as a
59	widget-tree factory**, decoupled from display:
60	
61	- `screenInit_X()` — builds the widget tree (+ registers any MGS-wired events).
62	- `screenShow_X()` — attaches its root(s) to layer(s) and raises the `X_OnShow` hook.
63	- `leAddRootWidget(wgt, layer)` / `leRemoveRootWidget(wgt, layer)` — **re-host** a root onto
64	  whatever Legato layer we want, independent of the index MGS authored it on.
65	- `screenGetRoot_X(lyrIdx)` — fetch a root to re-host or toggle visibility.
66	
67	So each panel is authored in its own clean MGS Screen, then the compositor assembles the
68	trees onto the layer set it manages. The screen's `OnShow` hook is that panel's
69	**composition root** — where it runtime-registers its widget event callbacks (the DI pattern;
70	see the 2026-06-25 journal entry on widget events being runtime-registerable while screen
71	lifecycle events are direct calls).
72	
73	## 4. Hardware layer budget
74	
75	| Legato layer | LCDC | Content | Lifecycle |
76	|---|---|---|---|
77	| 0 | BASE | active full-screen view (dashboard, …) | swappable (replace) |
78	| 1 | OVR1 | **nav drawer** | resident — attach once, persists across base-view swaps |
79	| 2 | OVR2 | **modal dialog** (song/mode select), sized to the dialog | shown/hidden; background stays live |
80	| — | HEO | camera | `video.c`, **outside Legato** |
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
32:## Decision log
43:| 2026-06-25 | **UI architecture: disable the MGS screen state machine and let the app own screen orchestration, so panels coexist as live, independently-interactive LCDC layers — `ui_manager` + per-screen modules. Authoritative design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md).** Confirmed in the Legato core that `_state.layerList` is global, `leUpdate` renders/updates **every** attached layer each frame, and `leInput` picks touch across **all** attached layers top-to-bottom — there is no "active screen" render/pick gate. The only thing enforcing one-screen-at-a-time was `le_gen_init.c`'s state machine (`legato_showScreen` tears down the outgoing tree). Turning it off (and working around the MGS dangling-`le_gen_init.h` bug with a `compat/` stub) means we attach multiple panels' roots to different layers and they're all live + interactive at once. **Model:** each panel is authored as its own MGS Screen used as a *widget-tree factory* (`screenInit_` builds, `screenShow_` attaches + raises its `OnShow` composition root); `leAddRootWidget`/`leRemoveRootWidget` re-host a root onto whatever layer we choose. Layers: dashboard=BASE/0, nav=OVR1/1 (resident → "same nav over every view" free), modal song/mode dialog=OVR2/2 (sized to the dialog so live dashboard telemetry shows around it); camera=HEO outside Legato. Two verbs — **coexist** (overlay-as-layer, background live) and **replace** (swap base view on layer 0) — chosen per interaction, both owned by `ui_manager`, so the choice is reversible. `compositor.c` is promoted to `ui_manager`; per-screen/overlay modules own only their widgets+wiring. **This supersedes the earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable / reveal-then-promote" idea in the doc** — that was a symptom of the state machine, now removed. | Greg's call to author nav + dialogs as separate MGS Screens (cleaner than overlapping layers in one Screen) collided with Legato's one-active-screen model; the resolution was to drop that model entirely rather than fight it, which the global-layerList facts make safe. Disabling the state machine also removes MGS's per-screen switch baggage outright (deleted code, not dormant) and hands us `screenInit/Show` directly. Live-coexistence (vs. freeze) was required because some dashboard telemetry must keep updating under the nav/dialog (the camera already self-updates on HEO). Per-screen modules + a `ui_manager` orchestrator keep each panel's wiring local (composition-root-per-screen) while one top-level module owns the scarce layer budget — matching the MCC-isolation idiom (own files via `user.cmake`). 3 UI layers + camera is the hard ceiling. | 
44:| 2026-06-25 | **The GFX Canvas regen pushed FreeRTOS `heap_1` past 40 KB → silent boot hang (zero DBGU output); raised `configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE` 40960 → 100000.** Symptom: after the canvas MCC commit (`ed54f37`), marvin produced no DBGU output at all — bisected to that commit (`8de7c64` working). Not the compositor (it was stashed), and not the XLCDC OVR setup (BASE/HEO use the identical `LCDC_ATTRE`/`WAIT_ATTRS_EQ(SIP)` pre-`Start` pattern that already works, so OVR is symmetric). Root cause: the canvas additions (the dynamic `GFX_CANVAS_Task` + extra OSAL/driver allocations on the 4-layer/canvas display path) tipped cumulative `pvPortMalloc` during `SYS_Initialize` past the 40 KB `heap_1`. Because `configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK=1` and `vApplicationMallocFailedHook()` is the MCC default (`taskDISABLE_INTERRUPTS(); for(;;){}`), the failed alloc spun with IRQs off **before** `APP_Initialize`/`log_init` (initialization.c:499) ran → no banner, indistinguishable from a dead board. **Two durable follow-ups (both carried):** (1) the heap size is **not** in `FreeRTOS.yml` — it's a raw literal in the generated `FreeRTOSConfig.h`, so the bump is an **MCC re-apply patch** (joins patch #8, also a `FreeRTOSConfig.h` edit) and will silently revert on the next regen → hang returns; set it in the MCC FreeRTOS component if it exposes Total Heap Size, else keep it on the re-apply list. (2) Patch `vApplicationMallocFailedHook` **and** `vApplicationStackOverflowHook` to emit a marker before the spin — a one-line DBGU write would have turned this multi-step bisect into an instant diagnosis. | Same silent-spin footgun already flagged for `vApplicationStackOverflowHook` (Open questions), now confirmed to bite via the malloc path too — heap exhaustion and stack overflow both present as identical dead-board hangs with the stock hooks. `heap_1` (never frees) is correct for marvin's static-allocation discipline, but MCC tasks + Legato OSAL still need it, so its size is load-bearing and must be tracked. 100000 is generous (+60 KB) headroom for now; right-size later once boot logs `xPortGetFreeHeapSize()`. Found by Greg's heap hypothesis after the XLCDC poll-loop theory was ruled out by BASE/HEO symmetry. |
```

```text
32	## Decision log
33	
34	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
35	|------|----------|-----------|
36	| 2026-06-29 | **Splash `.raw` is now generated by a committed script (`data/ui/make-splash.sh`), not by ad-hoc shell history; the raw byte order is `[A,B,G,R]` per pixel.** The XLCDC splash canvas is `GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888` whose pixel word is `0xRRGGBBAA` (`splash.c` `SPLASH_FILL 0x000000FF` = opaque black confirms it), so little-endian memory bytes are `[A,B,G,R]` — **not** Pillow's default `R,G,B,A`. The script splits channels and `Image.merge("RGBA",(a,b,g,r))` to get that order, resizes to 1280×800, and asserts the 4,096,000-byte size `splash.c` requires. Uses `uv` + Pillow (no ImageMagick/ffmpeg — neither is installed on this host). Verified empirically against the committed `splash.raw`: first pixel matched to within JPEG-re-encode noise, while the naive `R,G,B,A` ordering was fully reversed. Regenerated `splash.raw` from the (newer) `splash.jpg`, which had drifted out of sync. Documented in `data/README.md`; flash with `openocd/program-qspi.sh splash`. | The conversion step previously lived only in someone's shell history — undocumented and reproducible only by guessing the byte order (easy to get reversed, since the framework name "RGBA_8888" reads like Pillow's `R,G,B,A` but the little-endian word layout inverts it). A checked-in script with the size assertion makes the splash pipeline self-serve and drift-proof, and pairs with the existing `program-qspi.sh splash` provisioning step. |
37	| 2026-06-28 | **QSPI 8 MiB partition map locked — `flash/qspi_layout.h` is the single source of truth.** Splash blob `0x000000` (4 MiB) · UI assets `0x400000` (~3.98 MiB) · Settings ring `0x7FC000` (16 KiB / 4 sectors). All boundaries 4 KiB sector-aligned; contiguous, no gaps/overlaps. Splash at offset 0 (raw pre-decoded framebuffer; 4 MiB holds full-panel RGBA8888 = 3.91 MiB, or an RGB565 splash uses ~1.95 MiB — the reservation keeps both open, format decided when the loader is built). Read-mostly bulk grows upward; the small, frequently-erased settings ring sits at the very top as a stable anchor, **wear-isolated** from the bulk. Settings get 4 sectors (2× the 2-sector ping-pong minimum) for ring headroom. UI assets indexed by **compile-time offsets** for now (flashed with firmware); a manifest sector / littlefs can be carved from the front of the assets region later if assets must update independently. | One header (`qspi_layout.h`) means consumers and the `qspi` dev tools share offsets — no drift. Settings-at-top isolates erase wear and gives a fixed anchor independent of how the bulk grows. **Dev-tool caveat:** `qspi` smoke (last sector `0x7FF000`) and `qspi verify` (top-down) write into the settings region — destructive to it, but the ring-log's CRC-fallback-to-defaults makes that non-fatal (settings just reinitialize). Run heavy `qspi verify` before the settings store is populated, or accept a settings reset. | 
38	| 2026-06-28 | **QSPI read throughput — the serial clock (GCLK = 2×QSCK) was the lever, not per-access overhead. At 200 MHz GCLK (MCC max → 100 MHz QSCK), XDMAC mem2mem reads hit 18.2 MB/s → ~225 ms for a 4 MB splash, ~3× faster than SD (~750 ms). Read integrity verified at volume. Splash → QSPI via XDMAC mem2mem is GO.** Bench (`qspi bench`, `flash/qspi_smoke.c`) at 50 MHz GCLK → 25 MHz QSCK showed ~5 MB/s and I wrongly concluded "overhead-bound, clock maxed." Greg caught the datasheet note **GCLK must = 2×QSCK** and raised GCLK 50→200 MHz; everything scaled ~linearly (DRV_SST26_Read 4.6→14.8, XDMAC mem2mem 4.9→18.2 MB/s; the raw libc `memcpy` path stays ~2.5 — it is just bad on this region, ignore it). Read path = **XDMAC channel 1 mem2mem from `QSPIMEM_ADDR` (0x60000000)** — ch0 is the ISC histogram DMA, and the PLIB only tracks ch0, so we program ch1's registers directly. Integrity confirmed by `qspi verify 1024 4`: 1 MiB × 4 passes via **both** the driver and XDMAC, **0 mismatches** at 100 MHz, with a position-dependent pattern (catches misaddressing, not just stuck bits). **Two dead ends ruled out:** (a) making the QSPI window **cacheable** in the MMU **hangs** — cache-linefill bursts aren't serviced by the SMM slave (back out; XDMAC bypasses the MMU so it's unaffected); (b) **continuous-read mode (CRM)** only trims the instruction byte on *non-sequential* access, so it does nothing for bulk sequential reads. _**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-29 21:55:28Z)**_
```

Two good questions — and the answers fall straight out of "one master screen + state machine off":

**1. Persistent — you're right, not needed.** Persistence only mattered as a defense against the screen state machine tearing down a screen's widget tree on switch. With the state machine off *and* only one screen that's always shown, there's no switch and no teardown — nothing to defend against. We build `Marvin` once via `screenInit_Marvin()` (pre-scheduler, as today) and never destroy it, so the widgets are retained regardless of the flag. So: doesn't matter functionally; leave it at the default (non-persistent is fine). No code impact either way.

**2. OnShow — no, I don't need it.** Here's the reasoning:

- An `*_OnShow` hook is only generated/raised through the `screenShow_X` path, and it gave us a *composition root* in the old per-screen model. In the new model that role moves to **per-panel `_Setup()` functions** (`Dashboard_Setup()`, `Nav_Setup()`, `SongSelect_Setup()`) that `ui_manager` calls explicitly, right after `screenInit_Marvin()` — operating on the widget pointers MGS has already created and placed on their layers.
- None of our setup needs "after shown" timing — registering button callbacks, corner radius, `ButtonAA_Enable`, content binding all work on the built tree before anything is bound to a HW layer.
- MGS-wired widget events (the `event_Marvin_<widget>_OnPressed` callbacks) are generated independently of OnShow, so disabling OnShow doesn't cost us those.

So a single `Marvin_OnShow` would just be one generated hook I'd have to keep in sync, dispatching to the same per-panel setups `ui_manager` can call directly. I'd **leave OnShow off** and keep the composition root per-panel — cleaner and matches where `ui_manager` already does orchestration. Enabling it does no harm if you'd rather have the hook there, but I won't rely on it.

Net: for the `Marvin` screen, **non-persistent, no OnShow.** The only generated entry points I need are `screenInit_Marvin()` and `screenGetRoot_Marvin(layerIdx)`, plus per-layer widget pointers in `le_gen_assets.h`.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-29 22:02:26Z)**_

The structure is exactly right:

- **3 layers, each built directly onto its own Legato layer, content-sized:**
  - Layer 0 → `root0` full-screen → `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD` → `leAddRootWidget(root0, 0)`
  - Layer 1 → `root1` 320×800 → `Marvin_PANEL_NAVIGATION` → `leAddRootWidget(root1, 1)`
  - Layer 2 → `root2` 1100×660 → `Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT` → `leAddRootWidget(root2, 2)`
- **`LE_LAYER_COUNT` = 3, now derived** from the 3-layer Marvin screen (no `LayerBudget` hack — confirmed deleted).
- `screenGetRoot_Marvin(0|1|2)` returns the three roots.

```text
#ifndef UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H
#define UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* Boot splash — a full-screen raw RGBA8888 image, NOT a Legato screen.
 *
 * It owns its canvas surface and pixel buffer and knows how to load itself: the
 * image lives in QSPI NOR (flash/qspi_layout.h QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET, provisioned
 * with openocd/program-qspi.sh) as raw RGBA8888 pixels in the layer's native byte
 * order, so displaying it is a flash read straight into the canvas buffer (the
 * buffer the LCDC scans out) — no JPEG decode, no widgets, no Legato, no SD. Raw
 * over JPEG: a software full-screen JPEG decode cost ~1.5 s; raw trades ~4 MB of
 * flash for skipping it. Reading from QSPI instead of the SD card also drops the
 * SD bring-up out of the splash path — splash up in ~260 ms, no card needed.
 *
 * This module does the load only. ui_manager (the compositor) decides which
 * hardware layer the splash canvas is shown on and lights the backlight. */

/* Assign the splash canvas pixel buffer. Call once pre-scheduler, before the
 * canvas state machine runs. */
void Splash_InitSurface(void);

/* Read the splash image from QSPI NOR into the splash canvas buffer. Returns true
 * if it loaded; on a flash error the buffer is filled with an opaque fallback
 * colour and false is returned — either way the canvas is displayable. Uses the
 * SST26 driver; call from a task once the scheduler is running. */
bool Splash_Load(void);

/* The splash canvas id, so the compositor can bind it to a hardware layer. */
uint32_t Splash_CanvasId(void);

#endif /* UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H */
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-29 22:07:36Z)**_

Good question, and the answer is **yes, keep a canvas** — but only because it's the cheapest *correct* mechanism, not because the splash is a Legato thing.

The splash is just a static RGBA8888 buffer on one HW layer, so in principle you could bind it straight to an XLCDC overlay via the PLIB (the way `video.c` drives HEO). But the GFX canvas is already doing real work for it that we'd otherwise hand-roll: setting the layer framebuffer address, the **per-layer RGBA8888 color-mode poke** (the gotcha the journal documented), the enable + vsync attribute-latch handshake, and — most importantly — a **clean handoff**: at reveal we `gfxcHideCanvas(splash)` and then bind the nav canvas to OVR1, with the canvas framework owning that layer's state consistently across the swap. If the splash poked OVR1 directly, the framework's tracked state for OVR1 would be stale when nav later takes it — a real hazard for zero benefit. We have 8 slots and only 0/1/2 are Legato render targets, so a slot costs nothing.

So: **keep the splash canvas, just move `CANVAS_SPLASH` 2 → 7.** One-line change; everything flows from that constant (`splash.c` already reads it).

Now the canvas numbering is pinned by the model — canvas id *must* equal the Legato layer for the three layer-screens (`canvas[i]` ↔ layer *i*): `CANVAS_DASH=0`, `CANVAS_NAV=1`, `CANVAS_SONGSEL=2`, splash off on `7`.

Here's the migration I'll execute:

```text
206	static void ui_boot_task(void *param)
207	{
208	    (void)param;
209	
210	    /* PHASE 1 — splash, before any Legato work, as fast as the SD allows. */
211	    (void)Splash_Load();   /* loads the image, or fills the fallback colour */
212	    bind_canvas(Splash_CanvasId(), SPLASH_HW_LAYER, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, true);
213	    enable_backlight();
214	    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();
215	
216	    /* Splash is up — let the app start everything else (services + camera) now,
217	     * in parallel with the screen painting below, so it's all warm at reveal. */
218	    if (s_splash_shown_cb != NULL) { s_splash_shown_cb(); }
219	
220	    /* PHASE 2 — build + host the Legato screens behind the splash. Scene-graph
221	     * edits are guarded against the render tasks; the canvas/layer binds after
222	     * are GFX-canvas only (no root-list mutation) so they need no guard. */
223	    scene_edit_begin();
224	    init_screens();
225	    s_screens[UI_SCREEN_DASHBOARD].host();
226	    s_screens[UI_SCREEN_NAV].host();
227	    scene_edit_end();
228	
229	    /* Dashboard live on BASE (covered by the splash until reveal). The nav is
230	     * hosted + painting into its own canvas, but not bound to a layer yet — it
231	     * shares OVR1 with the splash, so it takes OVR1 only after the splash vacates
232	     * it at reveal. */
233	    bind_canvas(CANVAS_DASH, HW_BASE, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, true);
234	
235	    wait_render_idle();
236	
237	    /* Hold the splash a minimum time so a fast boot doesn't flash it away. */
238	    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
239	    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
240	    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }
241	
242	    /* REVEAL — cut over to the (painted) dashboard, then give the nav OVR1. */
243	    gfxcHideCanvas(Splash_CanvasId());
244	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(Splash_CanvasId());
245	    bind_canvas(CANVAS_NAV, HW_OVR1, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, false);
246	
247	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
248	}
```

```h
 *                         before the canvas state machine is RUNNING.
 *   SongSel_Setup       — position the canvas window (centered) and wire content +
 *                         events on the widgets MGS already built; call once after
 *                         screenInit_Marvin. */
void SongSel_InitSurface(void);
void SongSel_Setup(void);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
```

```c
#include "ui/screens/song_select/screen_song_select.h"

#include "ui/ui_manager.h"   /* CANVAS_SONGSEL, BASE_W, BASE_H */

#include "gfx/canvas/gfx_canvas_api.h"
#include "gfx/legato/legato.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Marvin.h"   /* song-select widgets */

/* The song/mode-select dialog is layer 2 of the Marvin screen; MGS sizes that
 * layer's root to the dialog (1100x660) and renders it into CANVAS_SONGSEL. The
 * canvas is smaller than the panel, so the canvas window places it centered on the
 * 1280x800 display. */
#define SONGSEL_W   1100u
#define SONGSEL_H    660u
#define SONGSEL_X   ((int)((BASE_W - SONGSEL_W) / 2u))   /* 90  */
#define SONGSEL_Y   ((int)((BASE_H - SONGSEL_H) / 2u))   /* 70  */

#define FB_NOCACHE   __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned (32)))

static uint16_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_songsel[SONGSEL_W * SONGSEL_H];

void SongSel_InitSurface(void)
{
    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_SONGSEL, SONGSEL_W, SONGSEL_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, s_fb_songsel);
}

void SongSel_Setup(void)
{
    /* Center the dialog. The root is already on Legato layer 2 (built by MGS); the
     * canvas window positions that layer's pixels on the display. Force a full
     * repaint so the panel is complete in the buffer before the compositor shows
     * the canvas. */
    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_SONGSEL, SONGSEL_W, SONGSEL_H);
    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_SONGSEL, SONGSEL_X, SONGSEL_Y);

    Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT->fn->invalidate(Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT);
}

```

```text
206	static void ui_boot_task(void *param)
207	{
208	    (void)param;
209	
210	    /* PHASE 1 — splash, before any Legato work, as fast as the SD allows. */
211	    (void)Splash_Load();   /* loads the image, or fills the fallback colour */
212	    bind_canvas(Splash_CanvasId(), SPLASH_HW_LAYER, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, true);
213	    enable_backlight();
214	    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();
215	
216	    /* Splash is up — let the app start everything else (services + camera) now,
217	     * in parallel with the screen painting below, so it's all warm at reveal. */
218	    if (s_splash_shown_cb != NULL) { s_splash_shown_cb(); }
219	
220	    /* PHASE 2 — build the Marvin screen + per-panel setup behind the splash.
221	     * Scene-graph edits (screenInit_Marvin's leAddRootWidget calls) are guarded
222	     * against the render tasks; the canvas/layer binds after are GFX-canvas only
223	     * (no root-list mutation) so they need no guard. */
224	    scene_edit_begin();
225	    init_screens();
226	    scene_edit_end();
227	
228	    /* Dashboard live on BASE (covered by the splash until reveal). Nav and
229	     * song-select are built and painting into their own canvases but not bound to
230	     * a layer yet — they take their layers at reveal, once the splash vacates. */
231	    bind_canvas(CANVAS_DASH, HW_BASE, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, true);
232	
233	    wait_render_idle();
234	
235	    /* Hold the splash a minimum time so a fast boot doesn't flash it away. */
236	    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
237	    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
238	    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }
239	
240	    /* REVEAL — cut over to the (painted) dashboard, give the nav OVR1 (bound but
241	     * closed/off-screen), and bring the song-select dialog up on OVR2 over the
242	     * live dashboard. (Initial bring-up: it shows at boot; open/close wiring and
243	     * the in-dialog song list come next.) */
244	    gfxcHideCanvas(Splash_CanvasId());
245	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(Splash_CanvasId());
246	    bind_canvas(CANVAS_NAV, HW_OVR1, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, false);
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-29 22:26:08Z)**_

You're right — widgets come from **Legato's** memory, not the FreeRTOS heap. Legato has its own:
- **variable heap** `LE_VARIABLEHEAP_SIZE = 524288` (512 KB)
- **fixed-heap block pools**: 16 B ×300, 32 B ×96, 64 B ×96, 128 B ×32, 196 B ×48, 256 B ×24 — widgets are allocated by size class from these.

So `screenInit_Marvin` building the combined tree could exhaust a **fixed-heap pool** (the Marvin screen has ~250 widgets). Crucially, `legato_config.h` (where these pool counts live) was **not** in your regen's staged set — so the pools are still sized for the *old* design.
```text
GFXC_RESULT _gfxcCanvasUpdate(unsigned int canvasID)
{
    gfxIOCTLArg_Value argValue;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerValue setBaseAddressParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerValue setLayerEnabledParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerValue setColorModeParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerSize setResParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerPosition setPositionParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerSize setSizeParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerValue setAlphaParm;

    if (canvasID < CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ &&
        canvas[canvasID].layer.id != LAYER_ID_INVALID &&
        gfxDispCtrlr != NULL &&
        gfxDispCtrlr->ioctl != NULL)
    {
        setBaseAddressParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        if (canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.pixels != NULL)
            setBaseAddressParm.value.v_pointer = canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.pixels;
        else
        {
            argValue.value.v_int = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
            gfxDispCtrlr->ioctl(GFX_IOCTL_SET_ACTIVE_LAYER, (gfxIOCTLArg_Value*) &argValue);

            gfxDispCtrlr->ioctl(GFX_IOCTL_GET_FRAMEBUFFER, (gfxIOCTLArg_Value*) &argValue);
            setBaseAddressParm.value.v_pointer = argValue.value.v_pbuffer->pixels;
        }

        setColorModeParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        setColorModeParm.value.v_uint = (unsigned int) canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.mode;

		//This is the physical resolution of the layer pixel buffer
        setResParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        setResParm.width = canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.size.width;
        setResParm.height = canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.size.height;

        setSizeParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        setSizeParm.width = canvas[canvasID].layer.size.width;
        setSizeParm.height = canvas[canvasID].layer.size.height;

        setPositionParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        setPositionParm.x = canvas[canvasID].layer.pos.xpos;
        setPositionParm.y = canvas[canvasID].layer.pos.ypos;

        setAlphaParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        setAlphaParm.value.v_uint = canvas[canvasID].layer.alpha;

#if (CONFIG_CANVAS_ENABLE_WINDOW_CLIPPING == true)
		//align offsets for non-32bpp frames
        if (gfxColorInfoTable[canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.mode].size != 4)
            setPositionParm.x &= ~0x3;

        if (setPositionParm.x < 0)
        {
            setBaseAddressParm.value.v_pointer += abs(setPositionParm.x) *
                    gfxColorInfoTable[canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.mode].size;

            setSizeParm.width += setPositionParm.x;
            setPositionParm.x = 0;
        }

        if (setPositionParm.y < 0)
        {
            setBaseAddressParm.value.v_pointer += abs(setPositionParm.y) *
                    setResParm.width *
                    gfxColorInfoTable[canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.mode].size;

            setSizeParm.height += setPositionParm.y;
            setPositionParm.y = 0;
        }

        if (setPositionParm.x + setSizeParm.width > displayWidth)
            setSizeParm.width = displayWidth - setPositionParm.x;

        if (setPositionParm.y + setSizeParm.height > displayHeight)
            setSizeParm.height = displayHeight - setPositionParm.y;
#endif

        //Lock layer and apply layer properties
        gfxDispCtrlr->ioctl(GFX_IOCTL_SET_LAYER_LOCK, (gfxIOCTLArg_LayerValue *) &setBaseAddressParm);
```

```text
void log_vprintf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, va_list ap)
{
    if ((int)lvl > (int)s_level) { return; }

    /* Take the mutex only when the scheduler is running and the mutex
     * was created. Pre-scheduler we're single-threaded so interleaving
     * isn't possible; xSemaphoreTake with portMAX_DELAY would hang
     * before vTaskStartScheduler. */
    bool locked = false;
    if (s_mutex != NULL
        && xTaskGetSchedulerState() == taskSCHEDULER_RUNNING)
    {
        if (xSemaphoreTake(s_mutex, portMAX_DELAY) == pdTRUE)
        {
            locked = true;
        }
    }

    (void)vprintf(fmt, ap);

    if (locked)
    {
        (void)xSemaphoreGive(s_mutex);
    }
}
    log_vprintf(lvl, fmt, ap);
    va_end(ap);
}
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
40	Per Microchip's GFX-canvas layer-screen guide¹, MGS is meant to be **one master screen whose
41	*layers* are the logical screens** ("layer-screens"), each auto-associated with its own canvas.
42	marvin currently *emulates* that by hand — each panel is a **separate 1-layer MGS Screen**,
43	built on layer 0 then manually disconnected and re-hosted onto another layer by `ui_manager`,
44	with `LE_LAYER_COUNT` pinned at 3 by a never-shown `LayerBudget` screen. We are migrating to
45	the framework's model: **one master screen named `Marvin`, one layer per panel** (dashboard,
46	nav, song-select, dialogs…). MGS then derives `LE_LAYER_COUNT` and associates each layer-screen
47	with a canvas, so the `LayerBudget` hack, the `compat/le_gen_init.h` stub, and the
48	disconnect/re-host dance all go away — `ui_manager` shrinks to buffer assignment +
49	`show_layer`/`hide_layer` verbs. **The splash stays separate and manual** (pre-Legato
50	RGBA8888 scanout) on a canvas slot *outside* the layer-screen range (0..N-1).
51	
52	> **§2–§4 below describe the per-screen-Factory + manual-re-host approach we are migrating
53	> away from.** They remain accurate for the code as it stands today; treat §0 as the target.
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-29 23:09:48Z)**_

Good thing to nail down. Let me lay out the three options honestly, because they're not equal.

**Option A — splash as an MGS layer-screen of Marvin: I'd reject this.** Two problems:
- **Boot timing.** The splash's whole value is showing in ~260 ms *while* the heavy `screenShow_Marvin` tree builds behind it. If the splash is a Marvin layer, its widgets don't exist until `screenShow_Marvin` runs — so it couldn't appear early. You'd have to split the build, which is uglier than anything we're trying to fix.
- **Impedance mismatch.** A layer-screen renders Legato widgets; the splash is a raw RGBA8888 blob from QSPI. You'd need a `leImageWidget` bound to a runtime buffer just to carry pixels Legato never touches — and it shifts the layer numbering (splash=0 pushes dash/nav/song-select to 1/2/3, `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=4) for no benefit.

So the real choice is **B (fully manual / direct XLCDC)** vs **keeping GFX_CANVAS but naming the slot**.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-29 23:11:52Z)**_

This actually makes the manual path the clear winner — it's far less code than I feared. The XLCDC PLIB exposes exactly the layer primitives, and **video.c already drives a layer this way** for HEO. Crucially, the `update` bool on each call handles the attribute-latch/SIP handshake that bit us during splash bring-up — so we don't hand-roll that.

**Recommendation: Option B — splash fully independent of Legato/GFX_CANVAS, direct XLCDC.** It matches reality (the splash is a pre-Legato raw blob, not a layer-screen), drops the magic canvas 7, and leaves the canvas pool as *exactly* the layer-screens (0/1/2). Show/hide is tiny, mirroring `video.c`:

```c
/* Splash_Show(OVR1) */
XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, false);
XLCDC_SetLayerAddress     (XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, s_fb, false);
XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos (XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, 0, 0, false);
XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYSize(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, BASE_W, BASE_H, false);
XLCDC_SetLayerEnable      (XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, true, true);   /* update=true → latch all */

/* Splash_Hide(OVR1) */
XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, false, true);
```

The hand-off to nav stays clean: `Splash_Hide()` disables OVR1, then `bind_canvas(CANVAS_NAV, OVR1, …)` reprograms OVR1 from scratch through GFX_CANVAS — no shared state, no ownership fight.

Refactor shape:
- **`splash.{c,h}`** — drop `gfxcSetPixelBuffer`/`Splash_CanvasId`/`Splash_InitSurface`; the buffer is just the static array. Add `Splash_Show(XLCDC_LAYER)` / `Splash_Hide(XLCDC_LAYER)` (ui_manager still owns the layer choice — passes `SPLASH_HW_LAYER`).
- **`ui_manager`** — delete `CANVAS_SPLASH` entirely; phase 1 calls `Splash_Load()` + `Splash_Show(SPLASH_HW_LAYER)`; reveal calls `Splash_Hide(SPLASH_HW_LAYER)` before binding nav.

Two small things to weigh:
- **Buffer address for the DMA:** `XLCDC_SetLayerAddress` wants the framebuffer's bus address — `s_fb` is in `.region_nocache` (DDR), same as the HEO buffer video.c hands it, so identical treatment. I'll confirm when wiring.
- **Regression risk:** the splash just stabilized, so this touches working code — but it's a contained swap (canvas calls → 5 PLIB calls) with a solid precedent, so risk is low.

Want me to implement Option B? If so I'll do it as its own commit on top of the migration so it's easy to bisect if the splash misbehaves.

```text
40	     * layer scans out — no SD mount, no decode (the blob is provisioned via
41	     * openocd/program-qspi.sh). The DRV_SST26 read sets up the QSPI memory-read
42	     * frame itself and completes synchronously; the poll is a bounded backstop. */
43	    DRV_HANDLE h = DRV_SST26_Open(DRV_SST26_INDEX, DRV_IO_INTENT_READ);
44	    if (h == DRV_HANDLE_INVALID)
45	    {
46	        LOG_WARN("SPLASH: QSPI open failed\r\n");
47	        fill_fallback();
48	        return false;
49	    }
50

52	    bool ok = DRV_SST26_Read(h, s_fb, sizeof s_fb, QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET);

55	        DRV_SST26_TRANSFER_STATUS st;
56	        uint32_t guard = 0u;
57	        do { st = DRV_SST26_TransferStatusGet(h); }
58	        while ((st == DRV_SST26_TRANSFER_BUSY) && (++guard < 4000000u));
59	        ok = (st == DRV_SST26_TRANSFER_COMPLETED);
60	    }
61	    DRV_SST26_Close(h);

63	    if (!ok)

66	        fill_fallback();
67	        return false;
68	    }
69
```

```h
#ifndef UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H
#define UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H

#include <stdbool.h>

#include "definitions.h"   /* XLCDC_LAYER */

/* Boot splash — a full-screen raw RGBA8888 image, NOT a Legato screen and NOT a
 * GFX canvas.
 *
 * It owns a static framebuffer and drives an XLCDC hardware layer directly (the
 * same way video.c drives the camera on HEO), so it can be on screen before
 * Legato / the Marvin screen is built — the image lives in QSPI NOR
 * (flash/qspi_layout.h QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET, provisioned with openocd/program-qspi.sh)
 * as raw RGBA8888 pixels in the layer's native byte order, so displaying it is a
 * flash read straight into the framebuffer the LCDC scans out: no JPEG decode, no
 * widgets, no Legato, no SD. Reading from QSPI keeps the SD bring-up out of the
 * splash path — splash up in ~260 ms, no card needed.
 *
 * ui_manager owns hardware-layer policy and passes the layer to show/hide on. */

/* Read the splash image from QSPI NOR into the framebuffer. Returns true if it
 * loaded; on a flash error the buffer is filled with an opaque fallback colour and
 * false is returned — either way the framebuffer is displayable. Uses the SST26
 * driver; call from a task once the scheduler is running. */
bool Splash_Load(void);

/* Program the given XLCDC layer to scan the splash framebuffer (full-screen,
 * opaque, RGBA8888) and enable it. */
void Splash_Show(XLCDC_LAYER layer);

/* Disable the given XLCDC layer. */
void Splash_Hide(XLCDC_LAYER layer);

#endif /* UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H */

```

```h
/* Boot splash — a full-screen raw RGBA8888 image, NOT a Legato screen and NOT a
 * GFX canvas.
```
